title: 20 startup mistakes John Rush regrets after building 30 startups in 20 years
summary: John Rush lists 20 regrets from 30 startups (VC-backed and bootstrapped). Core themes: stay lean and founder-led, validate before building, start paid in B2B, use boilerplates, and invest early in SEO, content and social media instead of chasing investors, partners and conferences.

principles.text: Don't chase VCs. Make users happy and investors will find you once you have traction.
principles.quote: So, don't chase VCs, just make users happy and VCs are gonna find you.

principles.text: Founders should do all the work until traction; employees take no risk, so no innovation.
principles.quote: Only founders have enough incentives to take risks. SO the founders should do all the work until they gain traction.

principles.text: Avoid teams of specialized developers; one fullstack dev beats a team until about $30k MRR.
principles.quote: Today I have 1 fullstack dev doing 5x more progress on a project than a team of 12 back then. Avoid "teams" at all cost until at least $30kmrr.

principles.text: In B2B, start with paid (30-day no-questions refund). Free tiers attract the wrong crowd and bad feedback.
principles.quote: Free projects attract totally wrong crowd with irrelevant feedback and drive your project away from where it should head.

principles.text: Use boilerplates instead of coding auth, admin and CRUD from scratch; speed went up 10x.
principles.quote: The moment I started using boilerplates, the speed went up 10x.

principles.text: Start SEO, blogging and social media early. An hour a day on blogging is enough, and he regrets starting X late.
principles.quote: I thought blogging is a full time job, but it's actually possible to spend an hour a day on it and still do a good job.
